draft.title: Why governments collect tax
card: Tax is money that people and businesses must pay to the government. Governments in Australia collect it from many sources.
Governments use tax to pay for services that many people share, such as hospitals, schools, roads and defence.
Tax also pays for support payments, which give money to people who need help, such as people who are unemployed or retired.
Without tax, governments would have little money to provide these services.
draft.remember: Tax is how governments get the money to pay for shared services and support payments.

a.q: What is the main reason a government collects tax?
opts: To pay for services like hospitals, schools and roads
To stop people from earning money from work
To give every business the same profit each year
To pay for goods that people choose to buy privately
a.why: Governments use tax to pay for shared services and support payments. Tax does not aim to stop people earning, and it does not pay for private purchases.
a.clue: Think about who pays for public hospitals and roads.

b.q: A new bridge is built over the Yarra River in Melbourne, and all drivers can cross it for free. Where did the government most likely get the money to build it?
opts: From tax collected from people and businesses
From fees paid only by the drivers who cross it
From the private savings of the workers who built it
From money the bank gave out without any limit
b.why: Governments pay for shared services like roads and bridges using tax collected from people and businesses. Drivers cross the bridge for free, so fees from them cannot be the source.
b.clue: The bridge is free to use, so who else pays?

a.best: To pay for services like hospitals, schools and roads

b.best: From tax collected from people and businesses

proposal.title: What tax is and why we pay it
card: Tax is money that people and businesses must pay to government. Paying it is not a choice: the law requires it.
Governments use tax to pay for services that everyone shares, such as schools, hospitals, roads and defence.
Many shared services, such as a public road or a public library, cost nothing to use. This is because tax has already paid for them.
Tax is collected from many people and businesses, so the cost of shared services is spread across the community. Without tax, governments would have little money to provide them.
proposal.remember: Tax pools money from many people and businesses to pay for services we all share.

a.q: Which of these best describes tax?
opts: Money people and businesses must pay to government
Money people choose to give to a charity they support
Money a business charges customers for what it sells
Money the government lends to people and businesses
a.why: Tax goes to government, and the law requires it to be paid. A gift to charity is a choice, and the price a business charges goes to the business, not to government.
a.clue: Think about who receives the money and whether paying is optional.

b.q: A new bridge is built over the Yarra River in Melbourne, and all drivers can cross it for free. Where did the government most likely get the money to build it?
opts: From tax collected from people and businesses
From fees paid only by the drivers who cross it
From the private savings of the workers who built it
From the profits of the shops near the new bridge
b.why: Governments pay for shared services like roads and bridges with tax collected from many people and businesses. Drivers cross the bridge for free, so fees from them cannot be the source.
b.clue: The bridge is free to use, so who else pays?
